description: Simulated annealing looks for a low-energy assignment of a QUBO model by flipping one bit at a time. It starts from uniform random bits; each *sweep* visits every variable once, in index order, and the Metropolis rule accepts a flip that does not raise the energy, and a rise `Δ` with probability `exp(−β·Δ)`. The inverse temperature `β` grows geometrically from a hot to a cold value over the sweeps: either given, or derived from the model so that the largest possible flip is accepted half the time at the start and the smallest nonzero coefficient once in a hundred times at the end. It returns the lowest-energy assignment it visited, not the last one, and a budget of flip attempts can pause a run that later resumes with the same result. It gives no optimality guarantee; use it when a model has too many variables to enumerate and a good assignment is enough.

papers.authors: S. Kirkpatrick, C. D. Gelatt, M. P. Vecchi
papers.title: Optimization by Simulated Annealing
